capitals.name: Ternate (Gammalammo)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Ternate', with 'Gammalammo (royal capital 1575-1606)'; Sultan Babullah made Fort Kastela his palace in 1575 (Ternate page). The Dutch built a fort at Malayo in 1607. Sultan Said was held in Manila after 1606. The pages name no other seat.

rulers.name: Baab Mashur Malamo (Momole Cico)
rulers.note: Reign table of the page; 'traditionally' from 1257.

rulers.name: Haji Muhammad Usman Shah
rulers.note: The table gives 1902-1915; the infobox has the final ruler dethroned by the Dutch in 1914. The table also lists Iskandar Muhammad Jabir Shah 1929-1975 and later titular sultans, after the state's end.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). 'established by Momole Cico, the first leader of Ternate, with the title Baab Mashur Malamo, traditionally in 1257'; the pages name no frontier, so the home island group and the facing Halmahera shore. Infobox area: none.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In the 1400s, Ternate also conquered neighboring islands such as the Sula Islands and Seram Island' (no year, confidence 1 in the ledger); the Sultanate page: the sultan 'held suzerainty over a realm shifting in size, usually including parts of Halmahera, Buru, the Ambon Quarter, the Sula Islands, and the east coast of Sulawesi'. The wider Babullah-era influence (1570-1583) is a vassal tint in the ledger, not part of this shape. The Spanish and Portuguese forts are occupation events.

correction.text: the home islands and the Sula Islands after the Ambon Quarter passed to the VOC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The princes of Ternate 'governed in the Ambon Quarter and were based on the Hoamoal Peninsula on Ceram up to 1656'; the Maluku page has 'the subordination of Ternate and Tidore in the 1650s'; the 1683 treaty cost 'more of his lands' (not named) and made Ternate a vassal of the Dutch. Halmahera-wide claims after 1824 (a Dutch residency) are not drawn.

region.text: Ternate island with Moti, Makian and the nearest Halmahera shore: the home of the kingdom

ledger.note: 1257: Momole Cico founds the Ternate kingdom. 'established by Momole Cico, the first leader of Ternate, with the title Baab Mashur Malamo, traditionally in 1257'; infobox 'Founded 1486' for the sultanate. The kingdom was earlier known as the Kingdom of Gapi (Ternate page).

union.text: western Seram around the Hoamoal peninsula (the Ambon Quarter), one part of the island Ternate 'conquered' in the 1400s

region.text: the Sula Islands and Seram, conquered 'in the 1400s'

ledger.note: c. 1400s: Ternate takes the Sula Islands and Seram. 'In the 1400s, Ternate also conquered neighboring islands such as the Sula Islands and Seram Island.' The page gives the century only; 1450 is the mid-point (page silent on the year); what the page calls Seram is drawn as its western part.

1486: Zainal Abidin makes the kingdom a sultanate. 'Zainal Abidin (1486-1500) enacted Islamic Law and transformed the kingdom into an Islamic Sultanate'; infobox 'Founded 1486'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: the Portuguese fort (Fort Kastela) on Ternate

ledger.note: 1522: the Portuguese begin their fort on Ternate. Construction of the Portuguese fort 'began in 1522' after Sultan Bayan Sirrullah 'brought them to Ternate in 1512'; hatched as a foreign-held post.

region.text: 'influence over most of the eastern part of Sulawesi, the Ambon and Seram area, Timor island, parts of southern Mindanao and Papuan Islands' (the Ternate city page adds the Banda Islands and the Solor Islands)

ledger.counterpart: Ternate's eastern dependencies (eastern Sulawesi, Ambon-Seram, Banda, Solor, Timor, southern Mindanao, Papuan Islands)
ledger.note: 1570: Babullah's reign opens Ternate's peak. 'The peak of Ternate's power came near the end of the 16th century, under Sultan Baabullah (1570-1583), when it had influence over most of the eastern part of Sulawesi, the Ambon and Seram area, Timor island, parts of southern Mindanao and Papuan Islands.' The page gives the reign span, not a year for the influence, and 'influence' is read as a tributary tint (soft).

region.text: the Portuguese fort (Fort Kastela) on Ternate

ledger.note: 1575: the Portuguese are expelled from Ternate. 'The Ternatans expelled the Portuguese in 1575 after a five-year siege' (the Ternate page: the Portuguese 'forced to capitulate to Sultan Babullah in 1575, who made the castle his palace'), after Sultan Hairun's murder in 1570.

region.text: 'influence over most of the eastern part of Sulawesi, the Ambon and Seram area, Timor island, parts of southern Mindanao and Papuan Islands' (the Ternate city page adds the Banda Islands and the Solor Islands)

ledger.counterpart: Ternate's eastern dependencies (eastern Sulawesi, Ambon-Seram, Banda, Solor, Timor, southern Mindanao, Papuan Islands)
ledger.note: 1583: Babullah dies and the peak ends. The reign table closes his reign in 1583; the page gives no year for the loss of the outer dependencies, so the end of the reign stands for it.

region.text: the former Portuguese fort and its surroundings on Ternate

ledger.note: 1606: the Spanish take the fort of Ternate. 'Spanish forces captured the former Portuguese fort from the Ternatans in 1606' and forced Sultan Said to settle in Manila; the Dutch returned in 1607 and built a fort at Malayo with Ternatan help, while Spain was allied with Tidore.

region.text: the Ambon Quarter and the Hoamoal peninsula of Ceram, governed by Ternatan princes 'up to 1656'

ledger.note: 1656: the Ambon Quarter passes to the Dutch. The princes of Ternate 'governed in the Ambon Quarter and were based on the Hoamoal Peninsula on Ceram up to 1656'; Hamzah and Mandar Syah 'did concede some regions to the Dutch East India Company in exchange for help controlling rebellions'; 'the subordination of Ternate and Tidore in the 1650s' (Maluku page).

region.text: the fort the Spanish held from 1606

ledger.note: 1663: the Spanish leave Ternate. 'The Spanish abandoned Ternate and Tidore in 1663' (Ternate page); Tidore's page has the withdrawal decided in 1662 and carried out in 1663-1666.
1801: the British and Tidore take Ternate. 'In 1801, Ternate was captured by the British and Tidorese after a long siege'; the Peace of Amiens the next year let the Dutch retake their Maluku posts.
1802: the Dutch regain their Maluku posts after the Peace of Amiens (Tidore page: 'the following year'). The Ternate page does not mention the 1801 capture.
1810: the British occupy Ternate again. 'Ternate was seized and occupied by British forces in 1810 before being returned to Dutch control in 1817.'
1817: Ternate returns to Dutch control after the British occupation of 1810.

union.text: Ternate island with Moti, Makian and the nearest Halmahera shore: the home of the kingdom

ledger.note: 1914: the Dutch annex Ternate. The Dutch annexed the sultanate 'in 1914'; infobox 'Final ruler dethroned by Dutch: 1914'. Ternate had been the seat of a Dutch residency since 1824 (page).

union.text: Ternate island with Moti, Makian and the nearest Halmahera shore: the home of the kingdom

ledger.note: 1914: the Sultanate of Ternate ends. The last ruling sultan was dethroned by the Dutch in 1914; the page adds that the sultanate 'lapsed after his death in 1975'.

wars.name: Ternate-Portuguese war and siege of Fort Kastela

zones.text: the Portuguese fort (Fort Kastela) on Ternate

wars.outcome: The Ternatans 'expelled the Portuguese in 1575 after a five-year siege'; the garrison 'forced to capitulate to Sultan Babullah'.
wars.note: Sultan Hairun's murder 'at the hands of the Portuguese' (1570) began it; the page gives no month.

wars.name: Spanish capture of Ternate and the Dutch return
wars.outcome: Spain captured the fort in 1606 and took Sultan Said to Manila; the Dutch, allied with Ternate, built a fort at Malayo in 1607; the Spanish, allied with Tidore, 'abandoned Ternate and Tidore in 1663'.
wars.note: The dossier of Tidore is sultanate-of-tidore.

wars.name: VOC subordination of Ternate and Tidore (1650s)

zones.text: the Ambon Quarter and the Hoamoal peninsula of Ceram, governed by Ternatan princes 'up to 1656'

wars.outcome: 'the subordination of Ternate and Tidore in the 1650s' (Maluku page); the Ambon Quarter governed from Hoamoal 'up to 1656'; the 1683 treaty made Ternate a Dutch vassal.
wars.note: The 1650s span is the page's word; the Ternate page gives no 1652 or 1667 treaty.

wars.name: British capture of Ternate (1801 and 1810)
wars.outcome: British (with Tidore) took Ternate in 1801, returned it after the Peace of Amiens; British forces seized it again in 1810 and returned it in 1817.
wars.note: The 1801 capture is only on the Tidore page.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier for any date; island groups are drawn as discs. The Babullah-era dependencies are an influence, not a border.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Ternate. Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. Start: 1257 is traditional (the infobox's 1486 is the sultanate); predecessor 'Kingdom of Gapi' is Ternate's own earlier name. Territory is the weak part: the pages give no frontier. The peak dependencies (1570-1583) are 'influence' on the page, drawn as a tint with provinces that over-cover it, soft. 'Seram' is drawn as western Seram only because the Tidore page has East Seram under Tidore in places. The Ternate page has no hongi or 1652/1667 treaty; the 1683 treaty cost unnamed lands and a vassal status that belongs to the dutch-republic dossier. Sultan Hamzah (1627-1648) 'expanded its territory' (unnamed) and is not drawn. The reign table gaps (1801-1807, 1876-1879, 1915-1929) are the page's. Gazetteer names wanted: Seram, Sula Islands (Kepulauan Sula), Halmahera, Buru, Banggai, Makian, Moti, Hoamoal.
